title: ThreeJS is underrated
author: Fun_Mission_6974
selftext:
Honestly, I think Three.js is pretty underrated when it comes to gaming.

People don’t realise how much you can actually do with it. You can make 3D games that run straight in the browser without needing people to download anything.

You can build environments, physics, lighting, animations, particle effects and even multiplayer games. And the fact that it all runs using JavaScript is pretty impressive.

Obviously, it’s not going to replace Unreal Engine or Unity for big AAA games, but I think people overlook how powerful it is for browser games and smaller indie projects.

I also think there’s a lot of potential for developers who want to experiment with game development without having to learn an entire game engine straight away.

It’s not perfect, and performance can be an issue with more complex games, but there’s genuinely a lot you can do with it.

I just think Three.js deserves way more attention in the gaming space than it gets.

comments.author: Lumpy_Conference6640
comments.body:
Bruv. Three.js is the future. 

1. It's free, your earning potential is uncapped. All the big engines, you pay a tithe. It's free now.. find out if you make over x. It just a scam to lure you in. 

2. Unity and Unreal, are capped. They've been around forever. Three.js is new and constantly improving within the react series. Especially with all the attention it's getting. 

3. 100% portable. You're shoehorned into everything from cloud based games, to Linux handhelds. Consoles are going the way of the dodo, even before AI.

4. Interoperability, with RSI, and MCP, you can build tools on tools. I've already seen amazing builds on here. Idk how you capture that iterative focus, but if there was crowd merge of tools. It litteraly rebuild the gaming industry over night. 

It's beyond belief the era we live in.
